info.title: Tatakai Link v1 (M0)
info.description: PC <-> phone link served by apps/desktop-native/crates/tk-link and consumed by apps/android-native/core/link. Derived from docs/redesign/03-pairing-upscale.md (which in turn rewrites the Temple v1 contract), trimmed by review E6 and E7: NO mDNS / TOFU in M0 (pairing = QR or pasted code only), NO /v1/settings, NO events/handoff/control/sync/downloads, NO phone source and source channel, library = one user-chosen folder, non-recursive, listed with ffprobe (optional in M0; the url source is the one that matters). Every response carries the header `Tatakai-Link: v1`. Error bodies are `{"error":{"code","message"}}` with FIXED messages (no paths, secrets, tokens or pairing codes).

host.description: PC LAN IPv4 (from the pairing payload)

x-transport.tls: TLS 1.3 and 1.2 via rustls with the `ring` provider (no aws-lc), ECDSA P-256, ALPN http/1.1, no session resumption, max 64 connections
x-transport.server: Own CA generated on first start (%APPDATA%\Tatakai-Next\link\ca.{der,key}; key protected with DPAPI). Server cert SAN = every active LAN IPv4 + 127.0.0.1 + DNS localhost; re-issued when the IP changes.
x-transport.clientIdentity: The phone pins the SHA-256 of the CA DER. Client cert issued by the CA, CN = device_id, 365 days. Client key = software P-256 sealed at rest with an AndroidKeyStore AES-GCM key in noBackupFilesDir (review E4, same model as Enigmata TempleCrypto/TempleKeyVault); held in memory behind an X509KeyManager; exported as temporary PKCS#8 only when the M1 mpv engine needs it.
x-transport.mtls: Required on every route except POST /v1/pairing. Active device checked PER REQUEST. Unknown route with an authorized device -> 404 session_not_found. Undefined method on an existing route -> 405 without JSON body.
x-transport.revocation: In-memory list + file; effect <= 2 s; live connections of the device are closed.
x-transport.bodyLimits: Every JSON body has a per-route cap and must be fully received within 10 s of the headers (408 body_timeout, connection closed).
x-transport.bind: Private LAN interfaces only; never 0.0.0.0 on a Public Windows profile. The Windows Firewall rule (Private profile) is created ONLY from Settings > Link > "Allow on private network" with a UAC prompt, never on first launch (review E6).

x-pairing-payload.format: tatakai-link:v1?h=<ipv4>&p=<port>&ca=<sha256 hex of CA DER>&c=<10 Crockford base32>&x=<unix exp seconds>&n=<PC name, url-encoded>
rules: Not an HTTP URL; contains the pairing code, so it is never logged.
Single window of 5 minutes, single use, <= 5 failed attempts. Validation order: window -> CSR -> code.
The phone REJECTS payloads whose scheme is not exactly tatakai-link:v1 (e.g. tatakai-link:v0, enigmata-temple:*), expired payloads (x in the past) and malformed ones.
The phone verifies that the CA returned by POST /v1/pairing matches the pinned `ca` and that the issued cert contains its public key.
x-pairing-payload.qr: The phone scans it with CameraX + zxing (no Google Play services) or the user pastes the text; the paste option is always available.

x-ffmpeg.note: Contract for the desktop implementation, not an HTTP surface.
x-ffmpeg.protocolWhitelist: http,tcp,crypto (E6: `crypto` is required for #EXT-X-KEY AES-128 HLS). FFmpeg only ever reads the loopback fetcher, never an external URL.

rules: https only (http only if the "allow HTTP" setting is on); ports 80/443/8080/8443.

The fetcher resolves DNS itself, rejects loopback, RFC1918, CGNAT 100.64/10, link-local 169.254/16 and fe80::/10, ULA fc00::/7, multicast, 0.0.0.0/8 and cloud-metadata addresses, and connects to the already-validated IP (anti DNS-rebinding: a name that resolves public first and private later is rejected).
Redirects: max 5, every hop re-validated (a redirect to a private IP is rejected); Cookie and Authorization are dropped on origin change.

Request headers: allow-list Referer, Origin, User-Agent, Accept, Accept-Language, Cookie, Range; total <= 8 KiB; no CR/LF in names or values (a header containing CR/LF rejects the whole request); Cookie only towards the initial origin.

HLS playlists (master/media/#EXT-X-KEY/#EXT-X-MAP) are rewritten so every URI goes through the fetcher with the same policy (segments and keys alike). The rewriter REJECTS data: and file: URIs and any scheme other than http(s); playlists are capped at 2 MiB; depth master -> media only (no further nesting).
#EXT-X-KEY with an absolute URI to a host that the policy does not allow is rejected.
If the phone sends extension_id AND the PC has that extension installed, each host is also intersected with its network:domain:* permissions; otherwise only the generic policy applies.
Limits: 64 concurrent requests per session, 2 GiB per session, 20 s timeout per request; logs redacted (no query strings).

x-ffmpeg.jobObject: The FFmpeg process tree lives in a Windows Job Object and dies with the app.

x-profiles.pipeline: decode (FFmpeg, d3d11va -> software fallback) -> upscale (Anime4K 4.0 via libplacebo/Vulkan) -> frame generation (none by default; frc_amf on AMD only for p-anime4k-1080-fg2x) -> encode (h264_amf | h264_nvenc | h264_qsv | libopenh264) -> fMP4 HLS
x-profiles.measuredSustain: true | false | "unknown": 10 s benchmark on first use, stored. `p-none` is always available.

post.summary: Pair a device with the open pairing window
post.description: Body <= 16 KiB. Unreadable or invalid JSON -> 400 request_invalid, larger -> 413 body_too_large, not received in 10 s -> 408 body_timeout; none of these consume attempts. The window is closed BEFORE the certificate is issued.

get.summary: GPU, encoders and upscale profiles of the PC
Files of the PC library folder (OPTIONAL in M0)
get.description: One user-chosen folder, non-recursive (E7), metadata via ffprobe cached by (path, mtime, size). `id` = HMAC-SHA256(32-byte install salt, folder id || relative path) truncated to 128 bits, hex (32 chars). Paths are NEVER returned. If B5 does not ship it, M0 has only the `url` source.

delete.summary: Forget this device (revokes its own certificate)

post.description: Body <= 4 KiB. One active session per device: creating another closes the previous one (its resources answer 410) and increments `generation`. `session_id` is opaque (not a credential).

csr_pem.description: PEM PKCS#10, ECDSA P-256, CN = anything (the server assigns the device_id)

instance_id.description: New UUIDv4 on every server start; a client seeing another value treats its sessions as lost and creates a new one at its position.

client_fg.description: Whether the phone may apply its own frame generation on top (M3, experimental). Clients that do not receive it treat it as suppressed.

profile.description: A profile id from /v1/capabilities. Default = default_profile. Unknown -> 422 profile_unavailable.

UrlSource.description: An external stream resolved by an extension on the phone. FFmpeg never receives this URL: the SSRF fetcher does (see x-ffmpeg).

url.description: https (http only if the PC allows it); denied by policy -> 403 url_source_denied

headers.description: Allow-listed names only: Referer, Origin, User-Agent, Accept, Accept-Language, Cookie, Range. Total <= 8 KiB; CR/LF -> 400 request_invalid.
